Both zygotes carry 47 chromosomes
questions.why: Meiosis II nondisjunction gives one gamete an extra chromatid and the other one too few, so those zygotes end up at 47 and 45.

questions.stem: A proposal opens with a budget table listing a $40,000 auditorium upgrade, then describes a classroom where students share torn textbooks. The juxtaposition chiefly works to
options: show that the auditorium project is legally improper
make the district's priorities look misplaced without arguing it
show that the writer supports both expenditures equally
summarize district spending in a carefully neutral way
questions.why: Setting the spending beside the shortage invites readers to draw the judgment themselves, which persuades more than stating it outright.

questions.stem: Two true-breeding white-flowered strains are crossed and all the F1 plants have purple flowers. The F2 generation shows a 9:7 ratio of purple to white. Which explanation fits?
options: Two genes act in one pathway, and both dominant alleles are needed
One gene shows incomplete dominance, giving three phenotypes
The trait is sex-linked and expressed in only one sex
A single gene carries a recessive allele that is lethal
questions.why: A 9:7 ratio is the 9:3:3:1 dihybrid pattern with the three minor classes pooled, the signature of complementary genes in a single pathway.

questions.stem: A student's draft thesis reads: "School uniforms are a topic that many people have opinions about." Which revision turns it into an arguable claim?
options: School uniforms have been worn in many countries for decades.
Some students like uniforms, and some students dislike them.
Uniforms come up at many school board meetings each year.
Uniform rules can cut morning conflict, but only if students help choose them.
questions.why: Only the fourth option makes a specific, contestable claim with a condition a reader could dispute; the rest report that opinions exist.

questions.stem: A diploid cell with 2n = 6 completes meiosis. Which statement about the gametes it produces is correct?
options: Each gamete carries six chromosomes, half of them maternal
Each gamete carries three chromosomes in one of several combinations
Each gamete carries three chromosomes, all from the same parent
Each gamete carries twelve chromosomes after replication
questions.why: Meiosis halves the diploid number to three, and independent assortment of the three pairs yields several possible maternal-paternal mixes.

questions.stem: A survey asks: "Do you agree that the district wastes money on unnecessary programs?" A writer cites the 71 percent agreement as proof of waste. The strongest objection is that the question
options: was asked of too few administrators to matter
produced a percentage that cannot be averaged
builds its conclusion into the wording, so agreement proves little
should have been translated into other languages
questions.why: The question assumes waste already exists, so agreeing with it is not evidence that waste exists — a leading question manufactures its own result.

questions.stem: A PCR product is run on a gel beside a size ladder. The sample shows a single band that sits between the 500 and 600 base-pair markers. What has been established?
options: The sample holds no DNA, since only one band appeared
The DNA was cut into many fragments of varied sizes
The product is longer than every fragment in the ladder
A product of roughly 550 base pairs is present in the sample
questions.why: Migration distance tracks fragment length, so a band between two ladder sizes indicates a product of about the size between them.

questions.stem: A writer revises "The team lost, and the season ended, and everyone went home" to "The team lost. The season ended. Everyone went home." The revision chiefly
options: breaks the events into separate beats, giving each one weight
adds causal links among the three events described
makes the passage more conversational and less formal
clarifies which event the writer thinks mattered most
questions.why: Splitting the clauses into short sentences spaces the events out so each lands on its own instead of blurring into one chain.

questions.stem: A tumor suppressor gene is inactivated in one cell, and that cell begins dividing without the usual checks. Which best explains how the loss contributes to cancer?
options: It speeds up repair of damaged DNA in that cell
It converts the cell into one that produces gametes
It removes a brake on the cycle, so damaged cells keep dividing
It raises the rate of apoptosis in nearby tissue
questions.why: Tumor suppressors normally halt the cycle until damage is repaired; losing one removes that brake and lets mutations accumulate.

questions.stem: In a primary spermatocyte from a species with 2n = 46, one homologous pair fails to separate at anaphase I while every other pair separates normally. Which set of chromosome numbers best describes the four sperm produced?
options: Two sperm with 24 and two with 22
One sperm with 24, two with 23, and one with 22
Four sperm with 23 each, but two carry duplicate genes
Two sperm with 25 and two with 21
questions.why: A single pair failing to separate sends both homologs to one secondary spermatocyte and neither to the other; meiosis II then divides each normally, giving two disomic and two nullisomic sperm.

questions.stem: In a letter about classroom heat, a superintendent writes: "We have heard the concerns. We have read the emails. We have sat in the same hot rooms." What does that repeated construction chiefly accomplish?
options: It concedes that the district has been slow to act on earlier complaints
It claims shared experience while answering criticism with presence rather than policy
It shifts blame for the heat onto the families who filed the complaints
It signals that the writer considers the complaints exaggerated
questions.why: The parallel repetition puts the writer inside the complaint before any plan appears, buying goodwill while leaving the underlying funding decision untouched.

questions.stem: A child with trisomy 21 carries two maternal copies of chromosome 21 that differ at markers near the centromere, plus one paternal copy. Which event best explains the extra chromosome?
options: Nondisjunction of sister chromatids during maternal meiosis II
Nondisjunction of homologous chromosomes during maternal meiosis I
A mitotic error in the embryo that duplicated one maternal copy
Crossing over between chromosome 21 and chromosome 22 in prophase I
questions.why: Two different maternal homologs in one gamete means the pair failed to separate at meiosis I; a meiosis II error would deliver two identical sister chromatids instead.

questions.stem: A student argues that the district communicates openly, citing only the district's own press release about its new transparency policy. Which change would most strengthen the evidence?
options: Quoting the press release at greater length so its policy language is exact
Adding the superintendent's title and the date the release was issued
Naming the campus where the policy was first announced to reporters
Adding an independent audit or a reporter's account of records requests
questions.why: A source judging itself cannot establish openness; external records or independent reporting test the claim that the release merely asserts.

questions.stem: During anaphase I in one human oocyte, both homologs of chromosome 18 move to the same pole. The secondary oocyte is later fertilized by a normal sperm. Which outcome best explains the resulting karyotype?
options: 46 chromosomes, with one chromosome 18 exchanged for a maternal copy
45 chromosomes, because the second division ejects the extra homolog
47 chromosomes, with two maternal and one paternal copy of chromosome 18
46 chromosomes, because fertilization repairs the missing homolog
questions.why: The secondary oocyte already carries both chromosome 18 homologs, so adding the paternal copy yields three; meiosis II cannot correct an error made in meiosis I.

questions.stem: A speaker says: "Our opponents call this plan expensive. They are right that it costs money. What they will not say is what doing nothing has already cost us." What does the concession accomplish?
options: It grants a point the audience already believes, then reframes cost around delay
It withdraws the speaker's support for the plan until the budget is revised
It implies that the opponents have been dishonest about the plan's price
It concedes the plan is unaffordable and shifts to a purely moral appeal
questions.why: Conceding the uncontested fact costs nothing and makes the next move, measuring cost against inaction, sound like fair weighing rather than spin.

questions.stem: In a species with 2n = 8, one primary spermatocyte undergoes nondisjunction of a single pair at anaphase I, and both secondary spermatocytes then complete meiosis II normally. Which chromosome counts appear among the four sperm?
options: Four sperm, each carrying four chromosomes
Two sperm with five chromosomes and two with four
One sperm with five chromosomes and three with three
Two sperm with five chromosomes and two with three
questions.why: Both homologs of that pair travel together, so one secondary spermatocyte has 5 and the other 3; the second division splits each without changing the count.

questions.stem: An essay builds three long, clause-heavy sentences about a factory town's decline, then ends the paragraph: "The plant closed. The town stayed." What does that shift chiefly accomplish?
options: It quickens the pace so the paragraph ends before the point is clear
It introduces a topic the preceding sentences had not prepared for
It isolates the consequence, letting plain statements carry the verdict
It softens the earlier claim by making the outcome sound routine
questions.why: Short declaratives after long periodic sentences land like a summary judgment, and the rhythm makes an unremarkable fact sound like the conclusion.

questions.stem: One trisomic pregnancy is traced to a meiosis I error in the oocyte and another to a meiosis II error. Which observation would best distinguish the two cases?
options: The extra chromosome carries both homologs in the first case and identical chromatids in the second
The extra chromosome is maternal in the first case and paternal in the second one
The first case yields a live birth while the second always ends in miscarriage
The first case shows a translocation while the second shows a normal chromosome count
questions.why: Meiosis I separates homologs, so its failure puts two different versions in one gamete; meiosis II separates sister chromatids, so its failure duplicates one version.

questions.stem: A draft thesis reads: "Later start times would help students because sleep matters." Which revision makes the claim most arguable and defensible for a school board?
options: Later start times are the single change our district needs most urgently
Moving the first bell to 8:30 would raise attendance by ending forced early waking
Many students and parents agree that school starts far too early each morning
Sleep matters for learning, and later start times are worth considering
questions.why: The revision names a specific change, a mechanism, and an outcome a board could dispute and check; the others assert urgency or consensus instead of a claim.

questions.stem: Recombination between homologs is unusually low along one chromosome pair in a woman's oocytes. Which explanation best links that observation to the elevated rate of nondisjunction at meiosis I?
options: Without chiasmata, homologs are not held together and can drift to one pole
Without crossing over, sister chromatids cannot separate, so meiosis II fails
Low recombination shortens the chromosome, so it is lost during anaphase
Low recombination duplicates the chromosome number before meiosis begins
questions.why: Chiasmata physically tether homologs until anaphase I; with fewer attachments the pair can drift to one pole, which is why age-related recombination decline tracks aneuploidy.

questions.stem: An op-ed reports results from a survey of forty parents at one campus and concludes that "the district's families overwhelmingly support the change." Which description of the flaw is most precise?
options: A small single-campus sample cannot support a claim about district families
The survey was conducted by parents who already favored the change
The word overwhelmingly overstates a result the writer never reports
Survey results cannot be used as evidence in an argument about policy
questions.why: The defect is scope: forty parents at one school do not represent the district, so the conclusion outruns the evidence regardless of how the survey was run.

questions.stem: Trisomy for chromosome 21 is regularly seen in live births while aneuploidy for chromosome 1 is essentially never observed. Which explanation best accounts for that difference?
options: Chromosome 1 is too small to be resolved on a standard karyotype after fertilization
Nondisjunction never occurs for chromosome 1 because that pair aligns more precisely
Chromosome 1 aneuploids are repaired by enzymes that edit the extra copy away
Chromosome 1 carries too many dosage-sensitive genes for a copy change to be tolerated
questions.why: The more genes a chromosome carries, the more an extra or missing copy disrupts development; chromosome 21 is gene-poor, so trisomy 21 can survive to term.

questions.stem: A writer describes a flooded classroom in specific detail, a warped door and a bucket under a ceiling tile, and then states the district's three-year repair budget. What does that ordering chiefly accomplish?
options: It establishes the writer's technical expertise on maintenance before giving the figures
It delays the budget figure so readers cannot compare it with the damage
It makes an abstract allocation feel like a response to a particular room
It suggests the damage is too minor to justify a large repair budget
questions.why: The concrete scene gives the reader something to hold before the number arrives, so the budget is read as an answer to that room rather than as a statistic.

questions.stem: Cohesin along chromosome arms is not cleaved at anaphase I, though centromeric cohesin is cleaved. Which consequence best explains why the homologs fail to separate in that division?
options: Sister chromatids separate prematurely, leaving each homolog without a partner
Chiasmata cannot be resolved, so homologs stay joined and move to one pole
The spindle cannot attach, so chromosomes are excluded from both daughter cells
Crossing over repeats, creating extra chromatids that cannot pair properly
questions.why: Arm cohesin holds the chiasmata that keep homologs associated; without its cleavage those links persist and the joined unit segregates together.

questions.stem: A speaker opens a school board comment with: "I am not here to relitigate last spring. I am here to ask one question about next fall." How does that opening work?
options: It concedes that last spring's dispute was the board's own fault
It promises a broader review of district decisions than the speaker delivers
It warns the board that the speaker will raise the spring decision again
It sets aside a dispute the board expects, narrowing the ask to one question
questions.why: Pre-empting the anticipated fight lowers the board's defenses and makes a single concrete request sound modest and answerable.

questions.stem: A trisomic karyotype shows two maternal copies of one chromosome that are identical at every marker tested, plus one paternal copy. Which meiotic error best fits that pattern?
options: A meiosis II error, because sister chromatids that fail to separate are identical copies
A meiosis I error, because homologs that fail to separate are still identical copies
A mitotic error after fertilization, because only mitosis copies a chromosome exactly
A paternal meiosis error, because the extra copy must have come from the father
questions.why: Meiosis I separates homologs, which differ at many markers; meiosis II separates sister chromatids, so its failure duplicates one chromosome exactly, matching identical markers.

questions.stem: In an essay on phone bans, which sentence functions as a qualified claim rather than an absolute one?
options: Phone bans probably help focus most in classes where instruction is already structured
Phones are destroying students' ability to concentrate on anything for long
Any school without a phone ban is failing both its students and its teachers
No serious educator still defends letting students keep phones in class
questions.why: Only the first sentence limits its scope with probably and most and names a condition, which is what makes a claim defensible rather than merely rhetorical.

questions.stem: A secondary oocyte from a meiosis I nondisjunction event carries both homologs of chromosome 13. It is fertilized by a normal sperm and the zygote begins dividing. Which karyotype and consequence pair is most likely?
options: 45 chromosomes; the zygote arrests before its first mitotic division
47 chromosomes; only some cell lines end up carrying three copies
47 chromosomes; trisomy 13 usually disrupts development before birth
46 chromosomes; one homolog is ejected during the first mitosis
questions.why: The oocyte already holds two homologs, so fertilization yields 47; trisomy 13 is usually lethal in utero because the dosage imbalance affects many systems at once.

questions.stem: A student's counterargument paragraph reads: "Some people say later start times hurt athletics. But athletics are not the only thing that matters." Which revision makes the rebuttal strongest?
options: Restating the opposing view in stronger terms before dismissing it as narrow
Granting the scheduling conflict, then showing how practice times could shift
Removing the counterargument so the essay's own claim stands unchallenged
Adding that athletes are a small group whose needs can safely be deferred
questions.why: A rebuttal has to answer the strongest version of the objection; granting the real conflict and solving it does that, while dismissing the group does not.

questions.stem: A species has 2n = 6. One primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis I nondisjunction of one pair, and one of its secondary spermatocytes undergoes meiosis II nondisjunction of a different pair. Which statement best describes the sperm produced?
options: All four sperm carry an abnormal chromosome number for both chromosome pairs
Some sperm are abnormal for one pair, but no sperm carries both errors
Two sperm carry both errors because both divisions share one cytoplasm
No sperm are viable because two errors in one cell always halt meiosis
questions.why: The meiosis I error passes to both products of the first division while the meiosis II error affects only the other lineage, so the two defects never land in one sperm.

questions.stem: A writer addressing a school board about activity fees uses "we" throughout an essay about families who cannot afford them. What is the chief risk of that choice?
options: The pronoun makes the essay sound less formal than the board expects
The pronoun commits the writer to a position the board may reject outright
The pronoun implies the writer speaks for students rather than for parents
It presumes a shared identity that board members may not accept
questions.why: We invites solidarity but also claims common ground the audience may refuse; when the board reads itself outside that we, the appeal can sound presumptuous.

questions.stem: A karyotype of a conceptus shows 69 chromosomes rather than 47. Which event best explains a triploid result rather than a trisomic one?
options: Nondisjunction at meiosis I in the oocyte, followed by normal fertilization
Nondisjunction at meiosis II in the sperm, followed by normal fertilization
One chromosome pair failing to separate in the first mitotic division
Fertilization by two sperm, each contributing a haploid set to the egg
questions.why: Triploidy requires an extra full set of chromosomes; a nondisjunction event adds one chromosome, while dispermy adds an entire haploid genome at once.

questions.stem: An essay argues that a principal's silence after a budget cut was deliberate. Which sentence serves that argument best?
options: It was decided by the principal that no statement would be released
No statement about the budget cut was released by the principal's office
The principal let three weeks pass without a statement on the cut
A statement concerning the budget cut was never released to families
questions.why: The active construction names an agent and measures an interval, keeping responsibility visible; agentless passives make the same fact sound like something that merely happened.

questions.stem: In a 2n = 46 spermatocyte, one chromosome pair forms no chiasma and the two homologs remain unpaired until anaphase I. Which outcome best explains the gametes that result?
options: Both homologs are excluded from the spindle and degraded, leaving two sperm
The pair replicates again, so each sperm receives four chromatids of it
The homologs orient independently, producing sperm with 22 or 24 chromosomes
The unpaired homologs attach to another chromosome, producing a translocation
questions.why: Without a chiasma the two homologs share no orientation, so either can go to either pole, the classic route from failed pairing to aneuploid sperm.

questions.stem: A student's conclusion introduces a new statistic about district graduation rates that appears nowhere earlier in the essay. Which criticism is most accurate?
options: New evidence in the conclusion arrives unexamined and cannot be weighed
The statistic is irrelevant because graduation rates do not concern schools
The conclusion should instead repeat the introduction's thesis word for word
Statistics belong only in the opening paragraph of any argument
questions.why: A conclusion should synthesize what the body established; a brand-new figure has no analysis behind it and invites the reader to distrust the ending.

questions.stem: A person with Down syndrome has 46 chromosomes, one of which is a chromosome 21 fused to a chromosome 14. Which statement best distinguishes this case from ordinary trisomy 21?
options: The fused chromosome means no extra dosage of chromosome 21 genes is present
The fused chromosome carries chromosome 21 material, so dosage is still elevated
The karyotype shows monosomy 21, which produces the same features as trisomy
The fused chromosome necessarily arises from nondisjunction in the oocyte
questions.why: A Robertsonian translocation lowers the chromosome count while preserving two long-arm copies; the phenotype follows gene dosage, not the count printed on the karyotype.

questions.stem: A writer describes one girl's forty-minute walk to a school without a late bus, then argues that the district should fund afternoon routes. What does the specific account contribute?
options: It replaces the need for any budget evidence about transportation costs
It makes an abstract policy claim concrete enough to register as a stake
It proves that most students in the district walk to school each day
It shifts the argument from policy toward the girl's family circumstances
questions.why: One detailed case gives the policy claim a human referent and holds attention, but it illustrates the stake rather than establishing how widespread the problem is.

questions.stem: A mitochondrial inner membrane becomes freely permeable to protons while electron transport continues at a normal rate. Which outcome best explains what happens to ATP production?
options: ATP synthesis falls sharply because the proton gradient cannot be maintained
ATP synthesis rises because protons reach the matrix more quickly
ATP synthesis is unchanged because substrate-level phosphorylation continues
ATP synthesis stops only once oxygen has been fully consumed by the chain
questions.why: ATP synthase needs a gradient to drive phosphorylation; a leaky membrane dissipates it, so the energy from the chain is released as heat instead of stored as ATP.

questions.stem: Three sources are available: a district budget showing arts cuts, a parent survey reporting that students value arts electives, and a state report on arts credit requirements. Which combination best supports an argument that the cuts will delay graduation?
options: The budget and the parent survey, since both of them concern the arts
The parent survey and the state report, since both concern students
The budget alone, because it establishes the cuts most directly
The budget and the state report, because credits and cuts interact
questions.why: The argument needs both the size of the cut and the credit requirement students must still meet; the survey speaks to value, not to graduation risk.

questions.stem: A cell is placed in a hypertonic solution whose solute crosses the membrane slowly through channels. Which statement best predicts the immediate water movement?
options: Water enters the cell until solute concentrations equalize on both sides
Water movement stops at once because the solute is able to cross the membrane
Water leaves until the cell shrinks, and none returns as solute enters
Water leaves first, then partly returns as solute enters and the gradient falls
questions.why: Osmosis responds to total solute on each side; a slow leak does not prevent the initial efflux, and as solute enters, the gradient shrinks and some water returns.

questions.stem: A student writes: "Later start times raise transportation costs, so the district should not adopt them." Which revision best turns this into a qualified argument?
options: The district should not adopt later start times because costs matter more than sleep
Transportation costs are a serious concern that the district has never addressed
Costs rise, but a later bell may still be worth it if attendance gains offset them
Anyone who ignores transportation costs has not read the district's budget
questions.why: Qualifying means weighing an objection against a benefit instead of treating one cost as decisive; the revision states the tradeoff the argument has to defend.

questions.stem: In a large population mating at random, a recessive allele causing a mild trait is present at a frequency of 0.2. Which statement best describes its expected frequency after twenty generations with no selection?
options: It falls steadily because recessive alleles are hidden inside heterozygotes
It rises because recessive phenotypes reproduce more successfully than others
It stays near 0.2, with small random changes from genetic drift
It reaches zero once every carrier has been identified and removed
questions.why: Without selection, mutation, or migration, allele frequencies stay constant; only drift moves them, and in a large population its effect per generation is small.
